Let me analyze the two conflicts.

Axis 1: num
- register: "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 Rev. 2 Annex. 1"
- document: "R49/2006-FR2-09.07"

The document itself says "ANNEXE au certificat OIML N° R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev2". So the certificate number is R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev2, and this document is the Annex 1 to that certificate. The register carries the full identifier including "Rev. 2 Annex. 1" which specifies which document within the certificate family this record is (the annex, revision 2). The document text "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev2" — the "rev2" is present in document context too (the annexe title says rev2). The register's canonical form includes "Annex. 1" which denotes this is the annex document. Per rules: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." The document number clearly denotes the same certificate; the register's form is more complete/canonical (identifies the annex part). So verdict: same-entity, best_value = register's "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 Rev. 2 Annex. 1".

Axis 2: applicant
- register: "ITRON Indonesia"
- document: "PT Mecindo – ITRON Indonesia"

"PT Mecindo" is an Indonesian legal entity form (PT = Perseroan Terbatas, like "Ltd."). The document shows "PT Mecindo – ITRON Indonesia" which appears to be a relationship — Mecindo could be the local legal entity manufacturing for Itron Indonesia, or vice versa. Is this legal-suffix drift? No — legal-suffix drift would be like "ITRON Indonesia PT" vs "ITRON Indonesia". Here the document adds a genuinely different company name "PT Mecindo" joined with a dash. That's not a suffix drift; "Mecindo" is a different name entirely.

Options: same-entity (spelling drift, legal-suffix drift), document-noise (extraction artifacts, address fragments glued into name, OCR noise), different-entity (genuinely different company or person names = best_value = document's).

Hmm. Is "PT Mecindo – ITRON Indonesia" an extraction artifact where two names got glued together? It could be that the certificate lists "PT Mecindo" as the applicant with "ITRON Indonesia" as related, e.g., "PT Mecindo – ITRON Indonesia" as a joint name. But the rule for document-noise is about extraction artifacts like address fragments glued into a name or OCR noise. A dash-joined dual company name isn't obviously OCR noise; it reads like an intentional listing of a company with its affiliate/manufacturing site.

Genuinely different company names: "PT Mecindo" is a genuinely different company name from "ITRON Indonesia". But the document value contains both. If the certificate (legal instrument) names the applicant as "PT Mecindo – ITRON Indonesia", then the fused record should carry the document's value because the certificate is the legal instrument.

But wait — could this be a case where the register is right and the document glued two entities? The instruction says "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)." "PT Mecindo" vs "ITRON Indonesia" are genuinely different names. However, the document value isn't just "PT Mecindo" — it's the combined string. If we mark different-entity, best_value = document's = "PT Mecindo – ITRON Indonesia".

Alternatively, could it be document-noise? Document-noise requires "extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name, obvious OCR noise)". "PT Mecindo – ITRON Indonesia" doesn't look like an address fragment or OCR noise; it looks like a legitimate dual designation on the certificate. Actually, in real OIML certificates, sometimes the applicant is listed as the legal manufacturer with a brand. E.g., LNE certificate for Itron: applicant might be "PT Mecindo" (an Indonesian company, possibly an Itron subsidiary or contract manufacturer) with ITRON Indonesia branding. The dash suggests deliberate formatting.

Given the rules, the safest classification: different-entity — the document names a company (PT Mecindo) genuinely different from the register's "ITRON Indonesia", and per rule the document value wins because the certificate is the legal instrument.

Hmm, but "different-entity" semantics: "Genuinely different company or person names". The two values overlap ("ITRON Indonesia" appears in both), so are they genuinely different? The distinguishing part is "PT Mecindo". The document includes an additional legal entity name. The register truncated/dropped "PT Mecindo –". This looks like the register simplified the applicant name, dropping the legal entity "PT Mecindo". Since the certificate is authoritative, the fused record should carry the full document string.

Alternatively, one could argue it's "same-entity" if Mecindo is a legal-suffix-ish variant... no, "Mecindo" is not a suffix; PT is the suffix. "ITRON Indonesia PT" would be suffix drift. "PT Mecindo" is a different root name entirely. So different-entity.

Verdict: different-entity, best_value = "PT Mecindo – ITRON Indonesia", why: the certificate names a distinct legal entity (PT Mecindo) not derivable from the register's form; the document is the legal instrument so its fuller designation wins.
